follow-up time: Through the end of the 2013-2015 follow-up cycle (exact duration not specified)
exposure: Restricted to women at low risk of cesarean delivery based on maternal characteristics
cohort: 33,226 women participating in the Nurses' Health Study II who were born between 1946 and 1964
finding: Women born by cesarean delivery had a higher risk of obesity (multivariable-adjusted relative risk, 1.11; 95% CI, 1.03-1.19) and developing type 2 diabetes (multivariable-adjusted hazard ratio, 1.46; 95% CI, 1.18-1.81) during adulthood compared to women born vaginally.
mod_finding: Women born by cesarean delivery may have a higher risk of obesity and developing type 2 diabetes during adult life compared to women born by vaginal delivery.
